name: Rosa-Luxemburg-Stiftung Scholarship — International Study Scholarship (Studienwerk)
requiredDocuments: Certificate of enrolment (Immatrikulationsbescheinigung) for the relevant winter semester, stating subjects and number of semesters completed — or, if not yet enrolled, a current admission letter for the chosen programme
Tabular CV (in German or English, with full education history)
Proof of social/political engagement (e.g. confirmation letters / event programmes from political groups, parties, unions, associations, university bodies, NGOs)
One academic reference/assessment (Gutachten) from a lecturer/professor on your performance and study ability (German or English; no template provided)

Proof of highest educational qualification (e.g. bachelor's degree certificate) with final grade; non-German/English documents need an (uncertified) translation. If the bachelor's certificate is not yet available, submit a current transcript of records plus a university confirmation of successful completion (incl. thesis grade); the certificate may be submitted later
Current transcript of all academic records from the German university (if available)
Extract from the study regulations (Studienordnung) showing the standard period of study (Regelstudienzeit)
Identity card or passport (Personalausweis oder Pass)
Residence permit or visa for Germany (for non-EU nationals); a Fiktionsbescheinigung is not sufficient — may be submitted later by a stated deadline if delayed

Proof of German language skills at minimum B2 level (required even if your degree is taught in English); a current B1 certificate plus proof of enrolment in an ongoing/upcoming B2 course is also accepted at the deadline

timeline.resultsBy: Selection interviews with trusted lecturers (Vertrauensdozent*innen) run mid-December to February; funding begins 1 April
timeline.notes: Anchor date 2026-06: funding begins in the summer semester (1 April) of the following year, with a recurring 1 October deadline. The English application page documented the previous round (opened 20 Aug 2025, deadline 1 Oct 2025); the German required-documents page (Stand: Februar 2026, referencing Wintersemester 2026/2027) confirms the upcoming round, so the 20 Aug 2026 opening / 1 Oct 2026 deadline shown here is the projected next round based on the annually recurring 1 October deadline.

benefits: Monthly living-cost stipend (Lebenshaltungsstipendium) for international master's students, funded by the German Federal Foreign Office (Auswärtiges Amt); amount calculated according to BAföG rules
Income-independent study-cost lump sum (Studienkostenpauschale) of currently 300 EUR per month
Subsidies toward German statutory health- and long-term-care insurance (Kranken- und Pflegeversicherung), analogous to BAföG, for international scholarship holders
Child-care supplement (Kinderbetreuungszuschlag, analogous to BAföG) for scholarship holders with children, plus up to two semesters' leave
Extensive non-material support programme (ideelle Förderung): political-education events, summer schools, workshops, symposia, study trips and skills training
Grant does not have to be repaid (unlike BAföG)
mustKnow: NOT for applicants abroad — you must ALREADY be in Germany: enrolled (or at least admitted) at a state/state-recognised German university and residing in Germany for the purpose of study. You cannot apply from Bangladesh; this funds students who have arrived in Germany.
Master's only on the international-student track (no bachelor's; PhD is a separate programme). A COMPLETED bachelor's degree is required before the 1 October deadline.

GERMAN B2 IS MANDATORY — proof of German at B2 level is required even if your master's programme is taught entirely in English. A B1 certificate plus an ongoing/upcoming B2 course is accepted at the deadline.
Demonstrated social/political engagement aligned with the Rosa-Luxemburg-Stiftung's (left/socialist) aims is a core, evidenced selection criterion — not just academic merit.
You must plan to RETURN to your home country after completing your studies (return-home expectation; not a formal service bond).
You must NOT have been in Germany longer than 15 months at the time of application (exception: if you already studied in Germany, e.g. a bachelor's, or did targeted study preparation).
You must NOT be eligible for BAföG Section 8 (that group applies under the separate domestic-student track) and must be in Germany solely to study.
Living-cost stipend only: tuition fees are explicitly NOT reimbursed. German public universities generally charge no tuition, but private/fee-charging programmes would not have fees covered.
Direct application via an online portal only (no post/email); applications cannot be submitted on paper. The portal and full instructions are on the German-language pages.
Multi-stage selection with a mandatory interview with a trusted lecturer (Vertrauensdozent*in) between mid-December and February; no legal entitlement to funding.
You may work alongside the scholarship max 20 hours/week; international students funded via the Federal Foreign Office may earn up to the minijob limit within that rule without it being deducted.

universities: Any state or state-recognised German university (Universität or Fachhochschule)

duration: Up to the standard period of study (Regelstudienzeit) of the master's programme; funding begins from the 2nd master's semester
eligibleNationalities: Open to all foreign nationals worldwide (including EU nationals) who are not eligible under BAföG Section 8 — no country exclusion list. Bangladeshi nationals are eligible. Applicant must already be residing/enrolled in Germany.
languageRequirements: German at minimum B2 level is mandatory (proof required even for English-taught programmes). At the deadline, a B1 certificate plus proof of an ongoing/upcoming B2 course is accepted.
minGPA: Not specified as a numeric cutoff — 'excellent academic performance' / above-average achievement required
applicationFee: Free (no application fee stated; application is via the online portal)
bondObligation: No formal service bond, but applicants must plan to return to their home country after completing their studies
renewalConditions: Active participation in the foundation's non-material support programme and goal-oriented progress toward completing the degree are expected; funding lasts up to the standard study period (Förderungshöchstdauer = Regelstudienzeit)
